title: End of an era! #sleepnomore #immersive #immersivetheatre #theatre #Br...
transcript: Huge, heartbreaking theater news today. Sleep no more is closing in New York after 13 years and 5,000 performances. It's difficult to overstate the sheer influence, the monumental cultural impact that sleep no more is leaving behind. Sleep no more is simultaneously the gateway entry point for a lot of people into an entire art form, while also being widely considered the gold standard of that art form. The combination of which makes it this massive touchstone that everything else in its orbit is compared to. For better or for worse. I know some people who are deep in the immersive theater world who don't necessarily like that about it, and I personally do have some of my own criticisms of Sleep No more as a piece of storytelling. But it's impossible to deny how large the shadow of this production looms over the world of immersive theater and as an experience, how impressive the artistry behind it is. I've heard a lot of people say that the quality of the experience started to decline somewhat after the first couple years of its run, and I can't speak to that personally, cause I don't have that point of comparison. But I will say that from what I can tell, sleep no more, the scale and artistry of it are so impressive that I have to imagine that even in a state of decline, it is still kind of in a league of its own. I first went to Sleep No more In 2016 and then once more in 2018. And I've always intended to go back a third time. So keeping that promise to myself, I bit the bullet and bought a ticket for next month at the cheapest price point that they had. Which still hurt my wallet. Accessibility is not necessarily this productions strong suit. It was still a lot of money for me. I did not make the purchase lightly, but I decided that for me, it was worth it. Sleep no more is an institution as iconic in its sub industry as shows like Wicked Phantom and Lion King are to Broadway. With the added bonus of it being a completely different experience every time you go. If you've never gone, and if you can afford it, I. I do think you should seriously consider taking this final opportunity to experience this landmark work of art.
